description.from:
**What.** Publish DMARC for every sending domain (anth.us and mail.machines-on-machines.anth.us today) and have a place that receives the aggregate (rua) reports, so we can see who is sending as us and whether SPF and DKIM align. No DMARC record exists for either domain today (finding of 2026-11-12, see the parent story).

**What is needed.**
- A mailbox, or an aggregate-report service, that receives the `rua` reports and that someone reads. Owner: Ryan decides which (no mailbox exists yet, Ryan 2026-11-12). The address is configuration in AWS, never written into the repository (placeholders in specs).
- The `_dmarc` TXT record for each sending domain published through the DNS template in Git and applied by the pipeline. Never a hand-made record.
- Start at `p=none` with `rua` pointing at that mailbox; read the reports; tighten to `quarantine` (then `reject`) only when reports show SPF and DKIM aligned for every legitimate sender. The move to a stricter policy is its own reviewed change.
- If the mailbox is on a different domain than the one being reported on, the external-destination authorization record DMARC requires is part of the same template.

**Done when.** Each sending domain resolves a DMARC record from the template, a first aggregate report has arrived and been read, and the readiness check in the parent story passes its DMARC item.

**Why this is priority 1.** The Machines on Machines launch (PPY-f4b164) is blocked by this task, so signup cannot open without it.

**Owner decision needed (Ryan):** which mailbox or report service receives the DMARC reports.
